recommendation: Keep the external-repo audit commit for core. If OO wants further wording cleanup for SupplyRequest, SupplyDelivery, DeviceUsage, or DeviceDispense, make that change in the OO Incubator source/review process rather than in inactive core resource files.
issue_request: FHIR-7623 was Published/Not Persuasive with Modification for DSTU1. It requested distinct resources for patient-specific supplies versus stock supplies, including request and statement forms such as a wheelchair requested for or supplied to a patient; the approved disposition said the use case was covered by DeviceUseRequest and DeviceUseStatement and that SupplyRequest/SupplyDelivery scope and boundaries should be clarified.
initial_application: No FHIR-7623-tagged source commit was found. The old Supply resource was split into SupplyRequest and SupplyDelivery under the GForge #6067 family, and the 2016 pre-ballot SupplyRequest boundary update clarified that patient-focused medication/device requests should use DeviceUseRequest or MedicationOrder rather than SupplyRequest. Later FHIR-24936 and FHIR-27941 work refined the same DeviceRequest versus SupplyRequest boundary.
additional_context: source/fhir.ini now lists DeviceRequest and DeviceAssociation but has no active supplyrequest, supplydelivery, deviceusage, or devicedispense entries. Commit 3b38b80cf23f9cbb306fab8fcedb293315478c32 intentionally removed those OO resources from the core build and pointed references to the OO Incubator. The OO Incubator continuous build serves StructureDefinition JSON for SupplyRequest, SupplyDelivery, DeviceUsage, and DeviceDispense. Related boundary issues FHIR-24936, FHIR-27941, FHIR-37980, FHIR-46342, and FHIR-51689 already have combined-branch audit commits.
reconciliation: No core source files were changed. Editing source/supplyrequest, source/supplydelivery, or source/deviceusage would patch inactive copies, and the active core DeviceRequest/DeviceAssociation pages already preserve the patient-focused device request/association side of the original resolution.
